audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for vassal tribute, imprisonment, three-year siege, mass deportation, retrospective blame, child-through-fire, prophetic warning, Judah's inclusion, Assyrian population transfer, settler vulnerability, lions, imported priest, local and ancestral worship, and later Samaritan reception.

verses.restored: In twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king in Samaria over Israel and reigned nine years.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH, only not as kings of Israel who were before him.
Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him; Hoshea became his servant and returned tribute to him.

King of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and did not bring tribute to king of Assyria year by year. King of Assyria confined him and bound him in prison.
King of Assyria went up through all land, went up to Samaria, and besieged it three years.
In ninth year of Hoshea, king of Assyria captured Samaria, exiled Israel to Assyria, and settled them in Halah and Habor by river Gozan and in cities of Medes.
This happened because children of Israel sinned against YHWH their Divine, who brought them up from land of Egypt from under hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they revered other gods.
They walked in statutes of nations whom YHWH dispossessed from before children of Israel, and in statutes kings of Israel had made.
Children of Israel covered over things that were not right against YHWH their Divine and built high places in all their cities, from watchtower to fortified city.
They set up pillars and Asherim for themselves on every high hill and under every green tree.
There they burned incense at all high places, like nations YHWH exiled from before them, and did evil things to provoke YHWH.
They served idols, concerning which YHWH had said to them, You shall not do this thing.

YHWH warned Israel and Judah through every prophet and every seer, saying, Turn from your evil ways and keep my commandments and statutes according to all Torah I commanded your fathers and sent to you through my servants the prophets.
But they did not listen and hardened their neck like neck of their fathers, who did not trust in YHWH their Divine.

They rejected his statutes, covenant he cut with their fathers, and testimonies by which he warned them. They went after emptiness and became empty, and after nations around them, concerning whom YHWH commanded them not to do like them.
They abandoned all commandments of YHWH their Divine, made two cast calves, made an Asherah, bowed to all host of heavens, and served Baal.
They made their sons and daughters pass through fire, practiced divination and omens, and sold themselves to do evil in eyes of YHWH, provoking him.
YHWH became very angry with Israel and removed them from before his face; none remained except tribe of Judah alone.
Judah also did not keep commandments of YHWH their Divine but walked in statutes Israel had made.
YHWH rejected all seed of Israel, afflicted them, and gave them into hand of plunderers until he cast them from before his face.
For he tore Israel from house of David; they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king, and Jeroboam drove Israel from following YHWH and caused them to sin a great sin.
Children of Israel walked in all sins Jeroboam did; they did not turn from them,
until YHWH removed Israel from before his face, as he spoke through all his servants the prophets. Israel was exiled from its land to Assyria to this day.
King of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim and settled them in cities of Samaria in place of children of Israel. They possessed Samaria and lived in its cities.
At beginning of their dwelling there, they did not revere YHWH, and YHWH sent lions among them, which were killing some of them.

They spoke to king of Assyria, saying, Nations you exiled and settled in cities of Samaria do not know judgment/custom of Divine of land; he has sent lions among them, and look, they are killing them because they do not know judgment/custom of Divine of land.
King of Assyria commanded, saying, Bring there one of priests whom you exiled from there; let him go and live there, and let him teach them judgment/custom of Divine of land.
One of priests they exiled from Samaria came and lived at Bethel and taught them how they should revere YHWH.
Yet each nation made its own gods and placed them in houses of high places Samaritans had made, each nation in cities where they lived.
People of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, people of Cuth made Nergal, and people of Hamath made Ashima.
Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and Sepharvites burned their children in fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, gods of Sepharvaim.
They revered YHWH and made from all their people priests of high places, who made offerings for them in houses of high places.
They revered YHWH and served their own gods according to custom of nations from among whom they had been exiled.

To this day they do according to former customs. They do not revere YHWH and do not act according to their statutes, judgments, Torah, and commandment YHWH commanded children of Jacob, whom he named Israel.
YHWH cut covenant with them and commanded them, saying, You shall not revere other gods, bow to them, serve them, or sacrifice to them.
But YHWH, who brought you up from land of Egypt with great power and outstretched arm—him you shall revere, to him bow, and to him sacrifice.
Statutes, judgments, Torah, and commandment he wrote for you, you shall guard to do all days; you shall not revere other gods.
Covenant I cut with you, you shall not forget; you shall not revere other gods.
YHWH your Divine you shall revere, and he shall deliver you from hand of all your enemies.
But they did not listen and acted according to their former custom.
These nations revered YHWH and served their carved images; their children and children's children do as their fathers did, to this day.

translation_notes: Samaria's fall follows a three-year imperial siege and mass deportation. The theological retrospective must not erase Assyrian violence, civilian suffering, starvation, imprisonment, and forced population transfer.
Exile is not proof that displaced people deserved displacement. Communities under conquest must not be blamed for the violence an empire inflicted upon them.

The chapter critiques Israel and Judah through covenant theology, but its polemic against surrounding nations cannot authorize racism, xenophobia, colonial dispossession, or contempt for minority religions.
Children made to pass through fire are victims of adult religious and political systems. Child sacrifice is abuse and must never become a sensational marker of supposedly inferior peoples.

Assyria deliberately moves populations from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim into depopulated Samaritan cities. These settlers are also displaced subjects of empire, not voluntary invaders in a modern sense.
The lion account reflects ancient land-theology and danger in disrupted ecosystems. Animal attacks must not be preached as evidence that migrants practice the wrong religion.
The imported priest teaches a state-managed version of local religion. Imperial religious policy can control populations while appearing to accommodate them.

The resulting communities combine traditions. Mixed religious identity is described critically by the narrator but must not be used to persecute interfaith families, plural communities, or Samaritans.
Later anti-Samaritan prejudice and Christian supersessionism are categorically rejected. Samaritans are a living ethnoreligious community, not a synonym for corruption or half-faith.
The phrase 'to this day' belongs to the narrator's horizon and requires compositional audit.
safety_note: Do not blame exiles for deportation, stigmatize migrants or religiously mixed communities, preach animal attacks as punishment, or weaponize this chapter against Samaritans, Jews, interfaith families, or minority religions. Keep Assyrian colonial violence, child victims, displaced settlers, and the narrator's polemical perspective visible at the same time.
